lines.text: Have you ever noticed that tiny pinhole at the bottom of commercial airplane windows?
It is not a manufacturing defect; that tiny hole is a critical lifesaving safety feature.
Airplane passenger windows consist of three separate acrylic panes.
At thirty-five thousand feet, the air pressure outside is dramatically lower than inside the pressurized cabin.
The tiny hole, called a bleed valve, balances air pressure between the middle pane and the outer pane.
This forces the tough outer pane to carry all cabin pressurization stress, keeping the inner pane safe.
It also vents moisture to prevent your window from frosting over during flight.
